title: Prefix-aware grace periods and staleness proofing for KV eviction under continuous batching
creator: Marco Liu
description:
Summary:
We need an eviction policy enhancement that avoids pathological KV cache churn when continuous batching and aggressive GPU memory consolidation are active. Existing LRU/TTL approaches cause oscillation for long-running prefix-heavy workloads (e.g., multi-turn chat with pinned system context) and defeat GPU memory compaction heuristics. This ticket specifies a prefix-aware grace-period mechanism plus a lightweight staleness-proofing contract and verification harness to ensure correctness (no silent cache corruption, bounded staleness, and predictable reclaim latency).

Background:
- Continuous batching groups requests to maximize GPU throughput, but it increases the chance of interleaved prefix usage across batches.
- The KV cache holds shard-local KV frames stored in GPU memory with aggressive slab compaction to reclaim memory.
- Traditional LRU or simple TTL eviction either evicts useful prefix slices prematurely or retains stale/unreferenced prefixes and blocks compaction.

Goal:
- Implement a prefix-aware grace period that defers eviction of recently-referenced prefix slices for a short, configurable window aligned to batching epochs.
- Provide programmatic staleness proofs (lightweight metadata per prefix slice) that the runtime and tests can use to verify eviction safety (no use-after-evict in the serving code path).
- Integrate with GPU memory reclamation so compaction can consider grace periods and still proceed when global pressure requires hard reclamation.
- Add unit + fuzz + integration tests and a verification harness for CI to catch regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes configurable prefix_grace_ms and epoch_alignment flags in config
Under standard microbench suite we show >=25% reduction in prefix thrash events (metric: prefix_eviction_rebinds) on multi-turn chat workload
No increase in tail-latency P99 beyond 5% after enabling grace periods on dedicated GPU pools for 30-minute soak
Staleness-proof metadata is emitted with each eviction and verified by the test harness; no detected use-after-evict in CI fuzz runs
GPU compaction respects soft grace windows but performs hard eviction when memory pressure exceeds configured thresholds; documented fallback behavior present in runtime docs
proposed_design:
Design summary:
1) Epoch-aligned grace windows: Batching is already divided into epochs (continuous batching epoch ~ 5-20ms). We add a grace window that is quantized to these epochs (configurable multiplier). When a prefix slice is referenced, its 'last_ref_epoch' is set. The eviction decision considers (current_epoch - last_ref_epoch) and only schedules soft eviction if the difference >= grace_epochs. Soft eviction marks the slice as 'candidate' but does not immediately free the underlying gpu slab.

2) Staleness-proof metadata: For each slice we maintain a monotonic 'rev' (revision) counter written on mutation and a stable checkpoint token on pin/unpin transitions. The verifier uses revision & epoch to assert that any holder of a pin either has a rev >= the rev observed at eviction scheduling. If not, the verifier flags a potential race. The verifier runs in CI and as a lightweight runtime assert in debug builds.

3) Two-tier reclamation: soft and hard. Soft respects grace windows; hard is triggered by (a) global GPU free < threshold, or (b) slab fragmentation above threshold. Hard eviction performs atomic unpin + free with an eviction fence that signals pending RPCs. To avoid blocking serving threads, hard eviction is pushed to background threads with RAII-style pin guards.

4) Integration with kernel scheduler: When slices are candidates, we avoid moving them during in-flight kernel launches by holding ephemeral read pins until the kernel snapshot is taken. This prevents stale pointer reads after compaction.

5) Telemetry & invariants: emit prefix_eviction_candidate, prefix_soft_evicted, prefix_hard_evicted, prefix_rev_mismatch_verifier_fail metrics. Add a debug dump that includes epoch/rev/flags for forensic investigation.
tradeoffs: Increased metadata per slice (revision + last_ref_epoch) increases memory overhead slightly — measured ~0.6% increase in live GPU memory for typical workloads
Grace windows reduce eviction aggressiveness so worst-case memory pressure may force more hard evictions; tuning required per deployment tier
Verifier introduces additional assertions; debug builds catch races earlier but may impose overhead in CI fuzz runs
Complexity increases in eviction path and scheduler integration — more components to test and maintain
testing_plan: Unit tests for epoch quantization, last_ref_epoch update, and candidate transition
Fuzz harness that simulates continuous batching, concurrent pins/unpins, and forced compaction; runs nightly in CI with sanitizer enabled
Integration soak on dedicated GPU pool with multi-turn aggregator workload (48h) measuring prefix_eviction_rebinds, p99 latency, and memory high-water marks
Introduce a verifier mode in CI: after each test case, run the staleness-proof checker over recorded traces and fail on rev mismatches
Manual chaos: trigger hard eviction by lowering free-memory threshold and validate graceful degradation and telemetry
rollout_plan: 1) Feature gated behind config flags (prefix_grace_enabled=false by default). 2) Enable in internal staging for runtime-1.26 builds and run the 48h soak. 3) Enable on a small percentage (5%) of dedicated capacity for 72h with telemetry dashboards monitored. 4) Gradual ramp to 50% then global with regression kill-switch based on prefix_eviction_rebinds or p99 latency.

2026-03-11 Claire Donovan: Reviewed design; asked for clarity on rev counter rollover and overflow semantics. Suggested using 64-bit monotonic counter and explicit wrap handling in verifier.
2026-03-12 Aisha Raman: Implemented epoch field and last_ref_epoch updates in runtime WIP branch. Early unit tests passing. Planning fuzz harness next. Requesting review on PR #4821.
2026-03-13 Security Review (notes): If staleness proofs include any customer-identifying prefixes, strip or hash them before export. Security review required before enabling in private deployments.
